answer: Because the shale calculation reruns each epoch, the horizon weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the gale settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 118 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 53% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 15 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
